transcribed: read from the Cadetprep Excel sheet by extract-cadetprep.ts (sheet row = n); key and solution are the source's, kept as evidence

questions.stem: A is \(50\)% more efficient than B. Working together, they can complete a job in \(20\) days. How long would B alone take to complete the same job?
questions.keySolution:
Let B's efficiency = \(2\) units/day
A's efficiency = \(3\) units/day
Total efficiency = \(5\) units/day
Total work = \(5 \times 20 = 100\) units
B's time = \(100 \div 2 = 50\) days

questions.stem: A alone can finish work in \(70\) days. B is \(75\)% more efficient than A. How many days does B alone take to finish the work?
questions.keySolution:
A's efficiency = \(4\) units/day
B is \(75\)% more efficient, so B's efficiency = \(7\) units/day
Total work = \(4 \times 70 = 280\) units
B's time = \(280 \div 7 = 40\) days

questions.stem: The efficiency of A, B, and C is in ratio \(2:3:5\). A alone can complete work in \(50\) days. They all work together for \(5\) days and then C leaves. In how many days can A and B together complete the remaining work?
questions.keySolution:
A's efficiency = \(2\) units/day, B = \(3\), C = \(5\)
Total work = \(2 \times 50 = 100\) units
Work done in \(5\) days = \((2+3+5) \times 5 = 50\) units
Remaining work = \(50\) units
Time by A and B = \(50 \div (2+3) = 10\) days

questions.stem: A and B together can do work in \(50\) days. If A is \(40\)% less efficient than B, in how many days can A working alone complete \(60\)% of the work?
questions.keySolution:
Let B's efficiency = \(5\) units, A's efficiency = \(3\) units
Total work = \(8 \times 50 = 400\) units
\(60\)% of work = \(240\) units
Time by A alone = \(240 \div 3 = 80\) days

questions.stem: If A is \(6\) times more efficient than B, and B takes \(32\) days to complete a task, find the number of days required by A and B working together.
questions.keySolution:
B's efficiency = \(1\) unit/day, A's efficiency = \(7\) units/day
Total work = \(32\) units
Combined efficiency = \(8\) units/day
Time together = \(32 \div 8 = 4\) days

questions.stem: \(23\) people can do work in \(18\) days. After \(6\) days, \(8\) workers leave. How many more days will it take to complete the work?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(23 \times 18 = 414\) units
Work done in \(6\) days = \(23 \times 6 = 138\) units
Remaining work = \(276\) units
Remaining workers = \(15\)
Time = \(276 \div 15 = 18.4\) days

questions.stem: A can do work in \(15\) days, B in \(25\) days. They work together for \(5\) days, then A and C finish remaining work in \(4\) days. How many days can C alone finish the work?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(75\) units (LCM of \(15, 25\))
A's rate = \(5\) units/day, B's rate = \(3\) units/day
Work done in \(5\) days = \(40\) units
Remaining = \(35\) units
A does \(20\) units in \(4\) days, C does \(15\) units
C's rate = \(15 \div 4 = 3.75\) units/day
C alone = \(75 \div 3.75 = 20\) days

questions.stem: A man can do work in \(5\) days, but with his son's help, he can do it in \(3\) days. In what time can the son do it alone?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(15\) units (LCM of \(5, 3\))
Man's rate = \(3\) units/day
Combined rate = \(5\) units/day
Son's rate = \(2\) units/day
Son alone = \(15 \div 2 = 7.5\) days

questions.stem: A, B and C can complete work alone in \(20\), \(24\), and \(30\) days respectively. They start together. After \(2\) days, A leaves. Two days after A leaves, C also leaves. In how many total days will the work be completed?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(120\) units
Rates: A=\(6\), B=\(5\), C=\(4\) units/day
First \(2\) days: \(30\) units done, remaining \(90\)
Next \(2\) days (B+C): \(18\) units done, remaining \(72\)
B alone: \(72 \div 5 = 14.4\) days
Total = \(2 + 2 + 14.4 = 18.4\) days

questions.stem: Virendra's efficiency is \(M\)% of Surendra's efficiency, whose efficiency is \(N\)% of Upendra's efficiency. If ratio of time taken by Virendra to Upendra is \(5:2\), and \(M = 50\), find \(N\).
questions.keySolution:
Time ratio Virendra : Upendra = \(5:2\)
Efficiency ratio = \(2:5\)
Virendra = \(\frac{M}{100} \times \frac{N}{100}\) of Upendra
\(\frac{2}{5} = \frac{50 \times N}{10000}\)
\(N = 80\)

questions.stem: \(4\) men and \(7\) women can do work in \(8\) days. \(7\) men and \(4\) women can do the same work in \(5\) days. Find the number of days in which \(8\) women can finish the work.
questions.keySolution:
Let man's efficiency = \(x\), woman's = \(y\)
\((4x + 7y) \times 8 = (7x + 4y) \times 5\)
\(32x + 56y = 35x + 20y\)
\(x = 12y\)
Total work = \(440y\)
\(8\) women time = \(440y \div 8y = 55\) days

questions.stem: A and B together can complete a task in \(12\) days. If A alone can finish it in \(20\) days, how long will B alone take?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(60\) units (LCM of \(12, 20\))
A's rate = \(3\) units/day
Combined rate = \(5\) units/day
B's rate = \(2\) units/day
B alone = \(60 \div 2 = 30\) days

questions.stem: Renu works \(4\) hours/day for \(15\) days to complete a task. Seema works \(5\) hours/day for \(8\) days for same task. If Renu works \(2\) hours/day and Seema works \(4\) hours/day, with Renu working double the days of Seema, find days Seema works.
questions.keySolution:
Renu's total hours = \(60\), Seema's = \(40\)
Total work = \(120\) units
Renu's efficiency = \(2\) units/hour, Seema's = \(3\) units/hour
Renu's work/day = \(4\) units, Seema's = \(12\) units
Let Seema work \(x\) days, Renu \(2x\) days
\(8x + 12x = 120\), \(x = 6\) days

questions.stem: A, B and C can do work in \(30\), \(40\) and \(50\) days respectively. Beginning with A, if they work alternatively, in how many days will work be finished?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(600\) units
Rates: A=\(20\), B=\(15\), C=\(12\) units/day
In \(3\) days: \(47\) units
In \(36\) days: \(564\) units
Remaining \(36\) units done by A and B in \(2\) days
Day \(38\): A does \(20\) units, remaining \(16\)
Day \(39\): B does \(15\) units, remaining \(1\)
\(\frac{1}{12}\) of day \(40\)
Total = \(38\frac{1}{12}\) days

questions.stem: A and B work on alternate days with B starting. A alone takes \(24\) days. Work completes in \(11\frac{1}{3}\) days. In how many days can B complete \(\frac{7}{9}\) of work alone?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(24\) units
A's rate = \(1\) unit/day
A works \(5\frac{1}{3}\) days, does \(\frac{16}{3}\) units
B works \(6\) days, does \(\frac{56}{3}\) units
\(\frac{7}{9}\) of \(24 = \frac{56}{3}\) units
B completes \(\frac{7}{9}\) work in \(6\) days

questions.stem: A and B complete work together in \(20\) days, B and C in \(24\) days. If A is twice as efficient as C, find time for B alone to do \(40\)% of work.
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(120\) units
A+B = \(6\) units/day, B+C = \(5\) units/day
A = \(2C\)
Solving: C = \(1\), B = \(4\), A = \(2\)
\(40\)% work = \(48\) units
B alone time = \(48 \div 4 = 12\) days

questions.stem: Ajay and Bharat work alternately with Bharat starting. Ajay alone takes \(32\) days. Work completes in exactly \(8\) days. In how many days can Bharat finish \(7\) times the work alone?
questions.keySolution:
Ajay's rate = \(\frac{1}{32}\)/day
Ajay works \(4\) days, does \(\frac{1}{8}\) work
Bharat works \(4\) days, does \(\frac{7}{8}\) work
Bharat's rate = \(\frac{7}{32}\)/day
For \(7\) times work: \(\frac{7 \times 32}{7} = 32\) days

questions.stem: A is \(25\)% more efficient than B. B is \(20\)% more efficient than C. If C takes \(60\) days to complete work, how many days will A take?
questions.keySolution:
C's efficiency = \(1\) unit/day
B's efficiency = \(1.2\) units/day
A's efficiency = \(1.5\) units/day
Total work = \(60\) units
A's time = \(60 \div 1.5 = 40\) days

questions.stem: \(20\) workers complete work in \(15\) days working \(8\) hours/day. How many workers needed to complete same work in \(12\) days working \(10\) hours/day?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(20 \times 15 \times 8 = 2400\) worker-hours
For \(12\) days, \(10\) hours/day:
Workers needed = \(2400 \div (12 \times 10) = 20\) workers

questions.stem: A can complete work in \(36\) days, B in \(45\) days. They work together for \(10\) days, then A leaves. In how many more days will B complete the remaining work?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(180\) units
A's rate = \(5\), B's rate = \(4\) units/day
Work done in \(10\) days = \(90\) units
Remaining work = \(90\) units
B's time = \(90 \div 4 = 22.5 \approx 25\) days

questions.stem: A does \(\frac{2}{3}\) of work in \(20\) days. B does \(\frac{1}{4}\) of remaining work in \(5\) days. How many days will B take to complete the whole work?
questions.keySolution:
A does \(\frac{2}{3}\) work in \(20\) days
Remaining work = \(\frac{1}{3}\)
B does \(\frac{1}{4}\) of \(\frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{12}\) in \(5\) days
B's rate = \(\frac{1}{60}\) work/day
B takes \(60\) days for whole work

questions.stem: A machine can produce \(100\) units in \(8\) hours. Another machine is \(60\)% more efficient. How long will the second machine take to produce \(200\) units?
questions.keySolution:
First machine rate = \(12.5\) units/hour
Second machine rate = \(20\) units/hour
Time for \(200\) units = \(200 \div 20 = 10\) hours

questions.stem: \(15\) men working \(6\) hours/day complete work in \(20\) days. How many men working \(8\) hours/day can complete \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the work in \(12\) days?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(15 \times 6 \times 20 = 1800\) man-hours
\(\frac{3}{4}\) work = \(1350\) man-hours
Men needed = \(1350 \div (8 \times 12) = 1350 \div 96 \approx 14\)
Closest option is \(15\) men

questions.stem: A contractor estimates work will take \(100\) days with \(50\) workers. After \(40\) days, \(10\) workers leave. How many extra days beyond original estimate will be needed?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(5000\) worker-days
Work done in \(40\) days = \(2000\) units
Remaining work = \(3000\) units
With \(40\) workers: \(3000 \div 40 = 75\) days
Total time = \(40 + 75 = 115\) days
Extra = \(115 - 100 = 15\) days

questions.stem: A, B, C have efficiency ratio \(4:5:6\). If they work together for \(2\) days and complete \(\frac{1}{3}\) of work, how many days will A alone take to complete the work?
questions.keySolution:
Combined efficiency = \(15\) units/day
In \(2\) days, \(30\) units = \(\frac{1}{3}\) work
Total work = \(90\) units
A's efficiency = \(4\) units/day
A alone = \(90 \div 4 = 22.5\) days

questions.stem: Two workers A and B working together complete work in \(6\) days. If A is twice as efficient as B, how many days will the less efficient worker take alone?
questions.keySolution:
Let B's efficiency = \(1\) unit/day, A's = \(2\) units/day
Combined efficiency = \(3\) units/day
Total work = \(18\) units
B alone = \(18 \div 1 = 18\) days

questions.stem: A completes \(25\)% of work in \(5\) days. B completes \(40\)% of remaining work in \(6\) days. Working together, how many days to complete the whole work?
questions.keySolution:
A's rate = \(5\)%/day
B completes \(40\)% of \(75\)% = \(30\)% in \(6\) days
B's rate = \(5\)%/day
Together rate = \(10\)%/day
Time = \(100 \div 10 = 10\) days

questions.stem: A group of workers can complete a job in \(12\) days. After \(8\) days, \(\frac{1}{3}\) of workers leave. How many more days to complete remaining work?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(12\) units
Work done in \(8\) days = \(8\) units
Remaining work = \(4\) units
Remaining workers = \(\frac{2}{3}\) of original
Time = \(4 \div \frac{2}{3} = 6\) days

questions.stem: A can do work in \(16\) days, B in \(20\) days. They start together but A leaves \(4\) days before completion. In how many days is the work completed?
questions.keySolution:
Let work complete in \(x\) days
A works for \((x-4)\) days, B works for \(x\) days
\(\frac{x-4}{16} + \frac{x}{20} = 1\)
Solving: \(x = 12\) days

questions.stem: Machine A produces \(200\) units/hour. Machine B is \(50\)% less efficient. Working together for \(4\) hours, how many units do they produce?
questions.keySolution:
Machine A rate = \(200\) units/hour
Machine B rate = \(100\) units/hour
Combined rate = \(300\) units/hour
In \(4\) hours = \(1200\) units
